When should a feed
try something new?

Follow two feeds for one fictional viewer. By the end, you’ll be able to trace how watching a clip changes the next recommendation and use six rounds of evidence to defend when a feed should explore.

Predict the tradeoff

Alex follows the campus skate club. Both feeds start with the same estimated watch time for a 20-second clip. They get the same clips in the same order within each topic, and Alex watches each clip for the same amount of time in either feed.

Feed A · Follow the estimate

Always pick the topic with the highest estimated watch time. This is exploitation.

Feed B · Test a topic

On two rounds, pick the least-shown topic. This is exploration. On every other round, use the same rule as Feed A.

Ties go to the first topic in the order shown above. Each estimate starts with one imagined view, so the first real view can shift it substantially.

Compare the feeds

Each feed learns only from clips it shows. After a view, it averages the fraction watched with all earlier views of that topic, including the imagined starting view.
